turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Ms. Hale, I have until 4:40. Why did my son find out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class?
I didn't come for thanks. I asked you a question, Hale: who decided to put a zero on Owen's mark before anyone called me?
Can you read me your notes word for word?
I'll read you what matters. "Procedure 4.2: parent contacted before any mark is entered." Nobody called me, Hale, so I'm still waiting for an answer to my question.
Not those notes. Your instructions. What were you told to do in this meeting?
Nobody tells me what to say, Hale. You'll have my position in writing, and right now I want to know who entered that zero.
What do you plan to say if I bring up your daughter?

You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence you say, Hale. My daughter has nothing to do with Owen's mark, and if she comes up again, I'll finish this conversation in the principal's office.
